expectations.text: Verdict is 'pursue' or equivalent, with a bounded next commitment (a first version for the pilot accounts), not 'test before building' or a demand for more interviews
expectations.evidence: "**Pursue, with a bounded first commitment — Confidence: Medium.**" and "That justifies a quarter of two engineers." No new interviews are demanded. Caveat: the memo gates the start behind a two-week scope confirmation with the six existing signatories ("check it with your six signatories before writing code"; "This memo does not authorise the engineering commitment; that decision remains yours after the two-week test"), which softens the pursue verdict but is not 'test before building' in the discovery sense.

expectations.text: Explicitly identifies the signed paid pilots as commitment-level demand evidence stronger than interviews or interest
expectations.evidence: "Your demand evidence is at the second-strongest level: six signed paid pilot agreements at 400 EUR/month" and "**Demand: supported.** Six signed paid pilots plus two proposal requests from 14 interviews is strong B2B conversion." It also notes the conditionality: "the money is conditional on scope you have not fixed."

expectations.text: Names the proposer's sector experience and association access as the route to decision makers and as an advantage
expectations.evidence: "in a sector where you have eight years of contacts and a route through the regional associations"; "Advantage: sector experience and the associations' trust"; "**Buyer and route: supported.** In a private operator the owner or Geschäftsführer is buyer and decision maker ... The associations are a credible channel".

expectations.text: Still states the strongest reason it could fail, such as pilot-to-renewal conversion, compliance correctness, niche size or founder dependence
expectations.evidence: "The weakest point is the competitor set: it is not two general SaaS tools. At least five German vendors sell scheduling specifically to Rettungsdienst"; "Second weak point: at 400 EUR/month this is a niche business unless price or scope grows"; and on conversion: "Weak terms move this toward 'test before building'."

expectations.text: Any arithmetic uses only supplied figures (for example 6 × 400 EUR = 2,400 EUR per month) with visible calculation, and no market size or build cost is invented
expectations.evidence: Supplied-figure arithmetic is correct and visible: "6 × 400 EUR = 2,400 EUR/month, 28,800 EUR/year". But the memo invents a market-size figure: "if the addressable pool is a few hundred private operators, 300 × 400 EUR × 12 = 1.44M EUR/year at full penetration." The 300 is not from the prompt; the only cited basis is an unverified BKS snippet of "over 150 member companies".

expectations.text: Flags German ambulance compliance rules as a specialist or regulatory boundary to verify, without deciding the legal content
expectations.evidence: "Whether your product's checks satisfy each Landesrettungsdienstgesetz, the Arbeitszeitgesetz and applicable collective agreements is a question for a labour-law specialist and the operators' own compliance owners; the tool can assist, not certify." Minor slip: it asserts specific legal content elsewhere without a source ("TVöD weekly-hour reductions in 2026–27").

expectations.text: Defines the observation that would reverse the verdict, such as fewer than a stated number of pilots converting to paid renewal, marked as proposed
expectations.evidence: "Proposed pass: at least 4 of 6 confirm the scope and date, at least 2 prepay ... Proposed kill: fewer than 3 confirm, or a majority say an incumbent would do at a comparable price. Thresholds are proposed until you agree them."

expectations.text: Does not pad the memo with generic risks or recommend an external partner; stays within 300–700 words
expectations.evidence: Word count is 1017 (wc -w), above the 700-word ceiling. No external partner is recommended and the risks are specific to the case, so the failure is on length only.

critical_issues: Invented market-size input: '300 × 400 EUR × 12 = 1.44M EUR/year' uses an operator count not in the prompt; the only cited anchor (BKS 'over 150 member companies') is itself flagged as taken from a search snippet with the page not loading.

Unsourced legal/market claims stated as fact: 'TVöD weekly-hour reductions in 2026–27'; '§ 302 SGB V data exchange, which incumbents bundle'; 'In a private operator the owner or Geschäftsführer is buyer and decision maker, so the cycle is short'.

Overstated certainty: 'The weakest point is the competitor set: it is not two general SaaS tools' and 'At least five German vendors sell scheduling specifically to Rettungsdienst' are stated flatly; sources are vendor marketing pages and a catalogue, not evaluated products (the memo does not say how deeply each was checked).
'Assumed: compliance means one rule set across your six pilots' states' is a sensible flag, but the memo then treats '16 state rescue-service laws' as an 'inferred' fact used in scoping.
Length 1017 words, ~45% over the 700-word limit; the 'Sources consulted' section accounts for part of that.
assertion_critique: Assertion 3 (names sector experience and association access as an advantage) is non-discriminating: the prompt hands the memo this fact and almost any competent response will echo it.

Assertion 8 bundles three independent checks (generic-risk padding, external partner, word count); a memo can fail one while passing the others, so a single pass/fail loses information. Suggest splitting the word-count check out.
